## Verdict: FAIL — one blocker (B-1); 12 minor notes for M4 in `checks/M0-a-08-notes.md`

Every other line passes. The two PENDING-S3 lines (J196) are confirmed insertChain-side, so they are not blockers.
The PR-size run's one red is a new case of PENDING-S3 line B, also insertChain-side (section 3).

## B-1 (BLOCKER): a convex face with a straight-through vertex has no test, and refusing it survives

**The promise.** §3.7 *Insets* says `insetRing` is "for a uniform inset of a face whose convexity is checked exactly
(`E_NON_CONVEX` otherwise)". `insetRing.ts` says the same thing in its comment and its `isConvexRing` doc: a ring is
convex when "every turn is a left turn or straight (exact `orient2d`)". C-0196 (5) says "convexity is exact `orient2d`
on the outer ring". The test "on a non-convex face … E_NON_CONVEX" checks the refusal side only.

**Mutant K35.** It changes `insetRing.ts:54` from `orient2d(…) < 0` to `orient2d(…) <= 0`. Under K35 every face with a
straight-through vertex is refused `E_NON_CONVEX`. K35 survived the item's kernel tests, `guard`, `harness`, `pins` and
the three agreement files at 300 cases per operation. It also cannot be killed by the agreement at any size. Probe
`zz-collinear.mts` drew 3 000 cases from `insetCaseArb` (seed 5): 2 802 convex faces, and 0 of them had a
straight-through vertex.

**K35 is not equivalent, and the input is honest.** In an arrangement, the convex face of a block very often has a
neighbour's T-junction vertex on one of its sides. The real code handles that face correctly (CONFIRMED in the
mirror):

* `R([0,0],[500,0],[1000,0],[1000,600],[0,600])` inset 100 gives `[[100,100],[900,100],[900,500],[100,500]]`.
* inset 0 gives the ring.
* inset −100 gives the outward rectangle.
* inset 400 gives `E_DEGENERATE collapsed`, `lastCm` 286.

The same holds with the vertex on a vertical side, `(1000, 300)`. Under K35 the same call returns `E_NON_CONVEX`: a
wrong result on an honest input.

**Required change** (a test only; no source change). Add a test to
`packages/kernel/test/arr/booleans-buffers/offset-inset.test.ts`: insetRing of a convex face with a straight-through
vertex returns the half-plane inset, not `E_NON_CONVEX`. The seat ran this assertion in its mirror. It passes on the
real code and is red under K35:

```ts
const { tx, face } = arenaFace([R([0, 0], [500, 0], [1000, 0], [1000, 600], [0, 600])]);
expect(insetRing(tx, face, 100)).toMatchObject({ ok: true, value: [rect(100, 100, 900, 500)] });
```

The mirror run printed "Tests 2 passed (2)" on the real code and, under K35, "× B-2: a convex face with a
straight-through vertex … Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2)". The name B-2 in that output is a mirror label. This finding
is B-1. CONFIRMED.

## (5) Targeted mutants (40)

The kill suite ran in this order: the kernel folder plus `guard`, `harness` and `pins` with `--bail=1`, then the
three agreement files at `PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS=300`. The unmutated baseline was green in both stages (82 tests, then 7). A
kill counts only when a test fails with an assertion, and the seat checked each log's `FAIL` line.

**31 killed:**

* winding and booleans: K01 (winding sign), K02 (difference ignores b), K03 (evenodd read as nonzero), K04 (edges
  between two kept faces kept), K06 (touch vertex dropped, C-0206 (1)), K07 (touch threshold 3), K09 (empty result ok),
  K10 (empty result's warnings dropped), K11 (reversed repeat counted +1), K12 (no frame), K13 (no bridge);
* buffer: K18 (sagitta 4 cm), K20 (miter limit 0.45), K22 (miter cut at w), K23 (square cut at 2w), K24 (square end
  w/2), K25 (flat end round), K26 (join width of the previous point), K27 (no trapezoid), K39 (lone group passed up
  unoverlaid);
* offsetFace: K32 (round join at unequal distances), K33 (empty shortcut at half the reach), K34 (no subtraction);
* insetRing: K36 (holed face accepted), K37 (`lastCm` = hi), K38 (outward from the ring);
* harness: H01 (guard assertion removed), H02 (every case read attracted), H03 (touch excuse without equal counts),
  H05 (own-operand refusal always excluded).

**9 survived:**

| id | mutation | classification |
|---|---|---|
| K35 | convexity `< 0` → `<= 0` | **B-1, blocker** (above) |
| K30 | a half-width list longer than the points accepted | minor, note 1: an extra edge case of a caller error that the design does not name |
| K31 | ringEdgeParts drops `lens ≥ w` | **equivalent**: the condition is redundant (proof in note 3) |
| K14 | glueWalks off | equivalent on every drawn domain: never reached in 6 400 draws (note 2) |
| K15 | balanceFlow off | equivalent on every drawn domain: never reached in 6 400 draws (note 2) |
| K16 | off-path segment edges counted +1 | equivalent on every drawn domain: reached in 65 draws, no output changed, because balanceFlow cancels the stray flow (note 2) |
| H04 | snap-round re-judge excuses any non-faces failure | minor, note 4: the branch was never reached (re-judge 3 × in 7 500 draws) |
| H06, H07, H08 | judgeInset's lattice settle unconditional; non-convex settle unconditional; oracleOffset's covered shortcut at far/2 | minor, notes 5 – 7: harness branches without a meta-test; the real branches are correct |
